stem: A required pH reading was missed, but the technician remembers an approximate number. What is the strongest record practice?
choices: Backfill the remembered pH at the scheduled time and mark it as approximate.
Use the target pH because it represents what the solution should have been.
Use the controlled missing-data or late-entry process and do not present a remembered estimate as if it were the original contemporaneous measurement.
Copy the next available pH reading backward so the trend has no missing point.
rationale: A remembered approximation is not the same as a contemporaneous measurement. Backfilling it as if it were observed at the required time creates false precision and timing. The controlled missing-data or late-entry process preserves the fact that the original reading was missed while allowing any later context to be documented honestly.
